But wouldn't actually remove the old BeaconBlocksByRootV2 <@804047680195395675> I updated the 4844 readiness checklist today with (AFAICT) the latest links for all clients 👍 https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/Breakout-Room/4844-readiness-checklist.md Tim saw you comment on Twitter abt 4844 spec, specifically propagation in the CL making it impossible to implement on Polygon & BSC -- are other EVM-based chains also effected? Avax or Near for instance? Any EVM chain without a beacon chain can't do 4844 'as is' but this is also true of, say, withdrawals or even EIP-4399 got it; essentially this means rollups settling to other networks won't have differentiated fee mrkts (better resource pricing) and their rollups will be more expensive right? first part is correct, second part is hard to know (I have no idea what Polygon or Near gas prices are) if Near was 100x cheaper than L2s and 4844 make rollups 10x cheaper, then it might still be cheaper? makes sense, thanks! <@203220829473996800> Are this statements true for a tx of type blob tx? (fields from BlobTransaction container) - to field Union always of type Address (i.e. never None) - Always have empty data field - Always have empty access_list field

excerpts.content: Tim saw you comment on Twitter abt 4844 spec, specifically propagation in the CL making it impossible to implement on Polygon & BSC -- are other EVM-based chains also effected? Avax or Near for instance?

excerpts.content: Any EVM chain without a beacon chain can't do 4844 'as is'

excerpts.author: dapplion
excerpts.content:
<@203220829473996800> Are this statements true for a tx of type blob tx? (fields from BlobTransaction container)
- to field Union always of type Address (i.e. never None)
- Always have empty data field
- Always have empty access_list field
